## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.10 — diagnostics you can actually send

> **Alpha.** The Android APK is attached and has never run on a phone. This
> release exists largely to make that testable.

### Get a log off any device, with one button

**Settings → Diagnostics → Download.** One file: version, platform,
configuration, pairing and connection state, and the recent log. Attach it to
a bug report.

This replaces a flow that did not work in practice. The old `-debug` flag
assumed a command line to pass it on, a filesystem you could reach, and the
foresight to have enabled it *before* the problem happened. On a phone none of
those are true — and the alternative, adb, means putting a personal phone into
developer mode just to report a bug.

- **No restart needed.** Logs are now always buffered in memory, so a report
  can be produced after something goes wrong rather than before.
- **Three ways out**, because each fails somewhere real: Download, Copy, and
  View. A WebView can swallow a download; the clipboard API does not exist on
  a plain-HTTP page; text on screen always works. There should be no device
  where the answer is "you cannot get the log off it".
- **Never contains your auth token** — only whether one is set. The report is
  meant to be pasted into a public issue.
- **Only readable on the machine HueMux runs on**, since it includes your
  bridge address and local network details.

On Android the Download button hands the file to the system share sheet, so it
can go straight into an email or a chat.

### Testing the APK

`huemux-v0.0.2-alpha.10-arm64-debug.apk` is attached. Install it, and if
anything misbehaves, Settings → Diagnostics → Download and send the file. That
is now the whole process — no cable, no developer mode, no emulator.

Two things worth expecting, both known:
- **Bridge discovery is the most likely failure.** Android drops multicast by
  default; the app takes a lock to prevent that, but some ROMs filter it
  regardless. Manual IP entry is on the pairing screen and works.
- **Screen sync is absent.** No mobile browser can capture a screen, so it
  needs native `MediaProjection`, which is not built yet.
